title: Lexical Variation Across the Hispanic World

sections.content: You know *el carro* and *el auto* from B2 Unit 34, along with regional pairs such as *el departamento* and *el apartamento* or *la palta* and *el aguacate*. At C1, reading international press, academic essays, and fiction requires recognizing major transatlantic and inter-regional lexical pairs without treating either variant as an error.

A single concept may contrast a peninsular preference with a broad Latin American preference—such as *el coche* vs. *el carro / el auto* (car), *el ordenador* vs. *la computadora* (computer), *el móvil* vs. *el celular* (mobile phone), and *el zumo* vs. *el jugo* (juice). Both members of each pair are fully educated, standard words within their respective national norms (*normas cultas*). In formal writing or translation, the key rule is lexical consistency: adopt the vocabulary suited to your audience or institutional context and avoid mixing incompatible regional terms within the same paragraph.

sections.title: Transatlantic and Regional Lexical Pairs
rows: el carro (Mexico, Colombia, Caribbean) / el auto (Southern Cone) — el coche (Spain)
la computadora (most of Latin America) / el computador (Colombia, Chile) — el ordenador (Spain)
el vocablo / el sinónimo / el léxico / el americanismo

items.spanish: Tanto «la computadora» como «el ordenador» son vocablos plenamente aceptados en el léxico culto de sus respectivas regiones.
items.english: Both 'la computadora' and 'el ordenador' are fully accepted words in the educated lexicon of their respective regions.

items.spanish: En un congreso internacional, un hablante mexicano dirá «el carro» o «el jugo», mientras que un colega madrileño dirá «el coche» o «el zumo».
items.english: At an international conference, a Mexican speaker will say 'el carro' or 'el jugo', whereas a colleague from Madrid will say 'el coche' or 'el zumo'.

items.spanish: El diccionario registra numerosos americanismos que hoy enriquecen el vocabulario general de todo el mundo hispano.
items.english: The dictionary records numerous Latin American terms that today enrich the general vocabulary of the entire Hispanic world.

items.spanish: Al redactar un informe técnico, conviene mantener la coherencia léxica y no alternar «el celular» y «el móvil» en la misma página.
items.english: When drafting a technical report, it is advisable to maintain lexical consistency and not alternate 'el celular' and 'el móvil' on the same page.

sections.content: Watch grammatical gender when recognizing or quoting a transatlantic synonym: *la computadora* takes feminine articles and adjectives (*una computadora nueva*), whereas *el ordenador* takes masculine ones (*un ordenador*). Neither word is 'more correct' than the other; each is the natural standard in its region.
